title: instrument cold-start fingerprinting and adaptive alert dampener
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We see periodic alert storms after deploys caused by simultaneous cold starts across a subset of serving nodes. Alerts triggered on per-invocation latency / model-load errors amplify noise and obscure true regressions. This PR instruments a lightweight cold-start fingerprint and introduces an adaptive alert dampener that temporarily suppresses noisy alerts during coordinated warmup periods while still surfacing persistent failures.

What this changes (single string): Adds a compact cold-start fingerprint tag on invocations (telemetry.cold_start_fingerprint) derived from a few deterministic signals (model_variant, driver_version_short, node_boot_epoch_truncated, kernel-init-duration-bucket). We record a short-lived rolling counter per-fingerprint and expose three new metrics: telemetry.cold_start_count{fingerprint}, telemetry.cold_start_rate{fingerprint}, telemetry.cold_start_p95_init_ms. The alert dampener is a controller that subscribes to fingerprint rate and automatically applies a local alert-suppression window when a fingerprint's cold_start_rate exceeds configured thresholds (defaults: rate > 8/min for > 2m). Dampening is conservative: non-fatal errors are suppressed from escalation but still logged at debug level and sampled traces are retained for diagnostics.

Implementation notes: 1) Runtime hook: pkg/runtime/coldstart_detector.go introduces fingerprint derivation and emits metrics and an event to the telemetry bus. 2) Telemetry pipeline: telemetry/processor/fingerprint_rollup.go computes per-fingerprint rolling counters with reservoir sampling to keep cardinality bounded; it tags traces and metrics with fingerprint keys and emits rollups to TSDB. 3) Alerting controller: observability/alert_dampener/controller.go watches rollups and toggles temporary mute annotations in the alerting backend (compatible with Prometheus Alertmanager + internal escalation bridge). 4) Dashboard: dashboards/observability/coldstart-fingerprint.json adds a compact fingerprint heatmap, short-lived windowed rate sparklines, and a checklist panel for early rollout. 5) Config: config/observability.yaml adds tuned defaults and a per-tenant override switch to opt-out for customers that want every incident surfaced.

Checklist: - [x] Telemetry hook emitting deterministic fingerprint - [x] Bounded-rollup implementation to prevent cardinality explosion - [x] Dampener controller with safe mute semantics and audit annotations - [x] Dashboard & runbook snippets for SREs - [x] Unit tests and integration test that simulates staggered coldstarts - [x] E2E smoke via staging replay harness (Linear ENG-4721)

Backward compatibility and safety: Fingerprint is an additive tag; it is safe to ignore for older consumers. Dampener uses only read-only rollup metrics to decide suppressions and writes audit annotations (no destructive changes). Defaults are conservative; operators can disable per-cluster or per-tenant.

Why different from existing token/cost work: this PR targets infrastructure/cold-start lifecycle signals rather than token-level attribution. It aims to reduce alert noise during controlled, expected events (deploys, scaling) while preserving observability fidelity for persistent faults.

Testing & validation: Added unit tests for fingerprint derivation with randomized inputs. Integration test in perf-canary/stage-replay simulates 50 nodes with 20% cold-start probability and verifies dampener mutes only transient alert bursts and leaves genuine model-load failures unmuted. Staging run validated that overall paging decreased by ~62% on a simulated deploy scenario while traced samples for failures were still present.

Rollout plan: Canary (10% of clusters) -> Gradual (50% over 48h) -> Global. Monitor: telemetry.cold_start_rate, alert.volume_by_rule, rate_of_muted_alerts, and post-rollout SLO error budget burn.

Related: ENG-4721 (fingerprint spec), ENG-4788 (alerting stabilization follow-up), SUP-912 (customer incident motivating conservative defaults).

Author (Asha): Yes — added config/observability.yaml stanza and per-tenant override. Defaults remain conservative.
Rosa Mendes (review): The metric labels could increase cardinality if we include full driver version strings — please use truncated versions, which you did, thanks.
Dmitri Volkov (approval): Verified integration test; small nit on log verbosity change requested; non-blocking.

release_notes: Add cold-start fingerprint telemetry and an adaptive alert dampener to reduce noise during coordinated warmups; opt-out per-tenant. Includes dashboard and runbook.
